title: Mary, Mother of God (1 January)
hookLine: the year begins with Mary and, since 1968, the World Day of Peace

lines: THE YEAR BELONGS TO A WOMAN.
cards: Midnight on New Year's Eve: countdowns, fireworks, a phone buzzing with messages, resolutions. A few hours later, while plenty of people are still asleep, the Church holds a solemnity.
The first day of the calendar year belongs to a woman: Mary, under her boldest title, Mother of God. And since 1968, it has also been the World Day of Peace.
So the year opens twice: once with fireworks, and once with a mother and a prayer for peace.

teach.h: THE EIGHTH DAY, AND A NAME.
teach.b: January 1 is the octave day, the eighth day after Christmas. Luke says that on the eighth day the child was circumcised and named Jesus, and today's gospel returns to the shepherds at the manger.

They tell what the angels said, everyone wonders, and Luke turns to Mary: "But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart." While everyone else talks, she keeps and ponders. The day's title is a big one.

In the year 431, bishops met at Ephesus, in what is now Turkey, to settle an argument. Nestorius, a bishop of Constantinople, had resisted calling Mary Theotokos, God-bearer, preferring Christ-bearer.
The council insisted on Theotokos. It looks like an argument about Mary, but it was really about Jesus: if he is one person, truly God and truly human, then the woman who bore him bore God.
Catholic and Orthodox Christians use the title; Protestant churches generally accept the council's teaching about Christ, and some use the title, while speaking about Mary in their own ways.
In 1968, Pope Paul VI asked that the first day of every year be kept as a day of prayer for peace, and popes since have sent a message for it each year.

teach.h: THE LORD BLESS THEE, AND KEEP THEE.
teach.b: The first reading is the old priestly blessing from Numbers: "The Lord bless thee, and keep thee." A mother, a blessing and peace.
This week began with seven O's and ended here: o come, a light at midnight, the Word made flesh, the crib and the cross, Rachel weeping, an ordinary family, and now, begin with her.

how: Catholics keep January 1 as the Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God, a holy day of obligation in many countries, and the pope issues a message for the World Day of Peace.

games.q: you're a bishop at Ephesus in 431. one side wants to call Mary Christ-bearer only. the other, God-bearer. what does the council decide?
games.why: the council affirmed Theotokos. the point was about Jesus: the one she bore is one person, God and man.

practice: Bring to mind one place in the world with no peace tonight, and one place in your own life: a family fight, a cold silence, a grudge. Hold both, the big and the small, without trying to solve them.
If you pray, ask Mary's help or say the old blessing over that place, the Lord bless thee and keep thee; if not, simply wish peace to both.

wordCard.voice: Mary. The mother of Jesus, honored on January 1 as Mother of God, Theotokos, the one who kept all these words in her heart. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: God-bearer, the title affirmed for Mary at the Council of Ephesus in 431.

carryVoice: Your line: begin with her. A new year, opened with a blessing. Happy new year, and see you tomorrow.
